scope: Substantive refresh of an existing post at its URL, adding sources

observations.summary: Conventional (tank and gravel drainfield, typical single-family, large footprint); chamber (high groundwater, scarce gravel); drip distribution (dose tank and power); mound (shallow soil, high groundwater, shallow bedrock); recirculating sand filter (nutrient treatment, high water tables or near water); aerobic treatment unit (smaller lots, poor soil, sensitive surface water, regular maintenance); evapotranspiration (arid only); constructed wetland; cluster (two or more dwellings).
observations.inference_limit: Federal overview; local approval rules differ.

observations.summary: Inspect at least every three years; systems with mechanical parts generally once a year.

Conventional and enhanced treatment categories (intermittent sand filters, recirculating sand filters, trickling filters, NSF/ANSI certified proprietary units); new systems need enhanced treatment for reduced groundwater separation or fast or slow percolation; repairs for reduced groundwater or surface water separation, fast or slow percolation, under pavement, reduced dispersal area, existing seepage pits; nitrogen reduction for soils faster than 5 MPI in nitrate concern areas; new systems on undeveloped parcels not permitted within set stream distances; enhanced treatment requires maintenance contract, deed recordation, periodic inspection and annual fee.
observations.inference_limit: County summary table as amended 2022-08-16; parcel-specific approval depends on site evaluation.
